346130631da9: MultiDatePick returns several outputs, depending on what you are capturing:
142a8c46bd4f: A Text collection of ISO dates, ready to loop
309ed5d067f5: Consolidated ranges, when consecutive days should collapse into one record
9c116117e5cb: Two of those outputs are JSON, because Flow has no native type for "a list of objects with several fields each." You do not parse text in a formula. The package ships a Flow action, <t1>Parse Date Entries from JSON</t1>, that takes the JSON and returns a proper collection with From Date, To Date, Start Time and End Time. You loop that collection like any other.

041ff96588ea: One gotcha that costs people an hour
aabdbd838ec2: <t1>Set Config Name, not the checkboxes.</t1> The component has a long list of on/off properties, and in Flow Builder a checkbox input left blank is empty rather than false. You can skip all of it: build the calendar in the Setup Wizard, then put that config's name in the <t2>Config Name</t2> property. Every on/off setting then comes from the config, and the handful of flow-only ones (Required, Show Inline, Output Date Ranges as JSON) stay off unless you switch them on. Only if you skip Config Name and set everything by hand do you need <t3>$GlobalConstant.True</t3> or <t4>$GlobalConstant.False</t4> on the checkboxes you care about.
61ae3abaea2d: Drag the component onto the screen, set Config Name, save. No checkboxes.
386c7152336b: Want the component to save the records itself? Pass the parent record's Id into <t1>Parent Record Id</t1> and it creates one child record per date. Leave it blank to loop the output and create the records your own way.
9ae66c023fba: Decide the record shape before you build
b5543e56af63: The same nine selected dates can become nine records, or four records if consecutive days collapse into ranges, or one parent record with sub-blocks. Each is correct for a different report. Decide it before you build the flow, because changing it afterwards means migrating data as well as editing the flow.
